newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Dec 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Dec 16.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Former premier Anand Panyarachun and ex-Parliament president Ukrit Mongkolnavin have emerged as top candidates to clinch the Constitution Drafting Assembly's presidency after the political reform process moved a step foward yesterday with the nationwide election of prospective assembly members.

Both men are to be nominated by leading educational institutions for "specialist" seats in the CDA this week. Parliament will on Dec 26 pick 99 CDA members - 23 specialists from a total of 450 moninees and 76 from the 760 people who won the provincial elections yesterday. (The NATION)

- A tug of war between the New Aspiration and Chart Pattana Parties is looming, with the prime minister and Chatichai Choonhavan calling separate meetings with key economic officials at about the same time today. High-ranking government sources said the separate meetings were no accident, as both were aware of what the other was doing to build up their image as the leader that delivers on economic promises made in the election campaign. (BANGKOK POST)

- Free competition in Thailand's telecom sector is likely to come more quickly than expected. The telecom master plan providing for liberalisation in stages will be introduced sooner in line with trends worldwide, according to Transport and Communication Minister Suwat Liptapallop. (BUSINESS POST)
- The limited interest of Thai consumers in evironmentally-friendly products is the main reason manufacturers cannot sell their goods at competitive prices.

Although the private sector is aware of the global trend toward green products, there is little demand for this kind of product in Thailand, according to Pongvipa Lohsomboon, product manager for the Green Labelling Project, the body that issues green labels for manufacturers. (THE NATION)
